findings.desc: The branding smoke has a false negative: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:3353 still says "runCli — koala CLI 运行时入口", and packages/main/src/tasks/cli-engine-branding-smoke.ts:55 classifies any line matching /koala CLI/ as allowed. The new npm smoke passes (src unclassified=0 dist unclassified=0), so this scoped cleanup can leave a current CLI-engine branding remnant undetected. Narrow the allowlist to explicit legacy alias contexts or update the source/dist comment so the smoke fails on real Koala-branding remnants.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 88f311664: runCli runtime comment now says Lattice CLI; the broad koala CLI allowlist was removed; branding smoke now scans cli-engine and hooks src/dist and passes with all unclassified counts at 0.

findings.desc: Second hook branding fix is partial: cli-engine now announces [lattice-hook] at packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:3771,3818,3839, but the shared hook runner it immediately calls still emits [koala-hook] diagnostics at packages/main/src/core/hooks.ts:212,220,229,231,241,242 for internal error, timeout, failure, stderr, and success-with-stdout. Those are current CLI stderr lines a user can see, not legacy aliases or reviewer/process tokens, so hook output can still present Koala as the product identity. Migrate those hook-runner labels to Lattice or explicitly justify them as preserved legacy compatibility with evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 88f311664: shared hook runner diagnostics in packages/main/src/core/hooks.ts now emit [lattice-hook]; docs/guide-hooks.md was synced; branding smoke now includes hooks src/dist so this cannot regress silently.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/cli-engine-branding-smoke.ts:51 still classifies any line matching legacy.*koala or koala.*legacy. Because classification is line-level, a future user-visible current-product phrase such as "legacy cleanup: Koala is the current CLI" would be excluded from the unclassified count solely due to the word legacy. This leaves a hidden broad allowlist in the adversarial branding smoke; replace it with exact legacy annotations/tokens used by current source lines.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 202077355: removed the broad legacy.*koala/koala.*legacy allowlist and replaced it with exact legacy alias patterns; npm --prefix packages/main run build and npm --prefix packages/main run test:cli-engine-branding-smoke passed with all unclassified counts at 0.

findings.desc: F-003 broad allowlist itself is fixed: packages/main/src/tasks/cli-engine-branding-smoke.ts:50-53 now uses exact legacy alias patterns instead of legacy.*koala/koala.*legacy. But the hook guide still contains current-product/user-facing Koala wording that this story should clean: docs/guide-hooks.md:1 titles the guide "koala Hooks 指南", docs/guide-hooks.md:3 says "koala 在每条命令..." and calls it the koala framework, docs/guide-hooks.md:7 says "Koala 初始化", docs/guide-hooks.md:30 instructs users to run "koala session_brief", docs/guide-hooks.md:180 instructs "koala doctor", and docs/guide-hooks.md:192 describes koala self-observation. The smoke passes because FILES_TO_AUDIT is limited to cli-engine/hooks src/dist at packages/main/src/tasks/cli-engine-branding-smoke.ts:99-104, so this user-visible hook documentation branding gap is not caught.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit ce395d900: docs/guide-hooks.md now uses Lattice/lattice for current-product hook guide wording, preserving only explicit compatibility/config/env/path/example Koala tokens; cli-engine-branding-smoke now audits docs/guide-hooks.md and reports guide-hooks doc unclassified=0 after build and smoke rerun.
